title: Deep learning resolves subtle seismic-wave changes across the 2016 Norcia earthquake cycle
summary: A seven-layer convolutional neural network classified raw seismic waveforms recorded near Italy’s 2016 Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake as pre- or post-mainshock and separated time-to-failure intervals with over 90% test accuracy. The authors interpret the model’s performance, frequency dependence and null tests as evidence that local waveforms encode evolving attenuation and elastic properties consistent with progressive fault damage before rupture and postseismic recovery.
ai_technology: Seven-layer convolutional neural network trained on local seismic waveforms
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; Pennsylvania State University

evidence.tested: A seven-layer convolutional neural network classified raw seismic waveforms recorded near Italy’s 2016 Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake as pre- or post-mainshock and separated time-to-failure intervals with over 90% test accuracy.
evidence.unknown: Authors studied one earthquake sequence and state that generalization to other tectonic settings and prospective real-time precursor detection remain untested. Related changes in elastic properties were already reported by field studies; the paper's new contribution is applying deep learning to infer them from this local waveform sequence.
evidence.ai_role: Classified the waveform signals by their temporal relation to the mainshock; controlled tests using incorrect mainshock times, distant stations and filtered frequencies helped expose subtle local seismic-wave property changes associated with the fault cycle.
